name: Letta
summary: Open-source server for stateful LLM agents (formerly MemGPT) that persists agent state, memory blocks, and archival passages in PostgreSQL with pgvector, exposed over a REST API and SDKs. Deployable via Docker or usable as a hosted service, with agent state surviving context-window eviction.

agent-runtime.note: The Letta server runs the agent loop and persists all agent and message state in PostgreSQL, exposed through a REST API.

orchestration.note: Multi-agent coordination via shared memory blocks and message-passing tools, plus subagents and Schedules for recurring tasks.

knowledge-memory.note: Agents have editable in-context memory blocks plus archival memory with hybrid semantic and full-text search over pgvector.

tools-integration.note: Supports server tools, client-side tools, and MCP servers registered over streamable HTTP, SSE, or stdio transports.

identity-governance.note: Self-hosted access control is a single shared server password; the open-source server documents no role-based access control, approvals, or audit log.

observability.note: The Agent Development Environment surfaces agent reasoning, tool usage, and state in real time, but there is no documented cost accounting or failure queue.

data-secrets.note: The document/file source system is deprecated and disabled, and no encrypted secrets store is provided; credentials are server environment variables.

evaluation.note: No datasets, scorers, or evaluation-run functionality is documented.

channels.note: Built-in channel adapters connect agents to Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, and Signal, plus a web and desktop chat UI.

code-execution.note: Custom server tools execute in an E2B sandbox requiring external API credentials; there is no general-purpose code interpreter or terminal runtime built in.

human-in-loop.note: Tools marked requires_approval halt the agent and emit an approval request with tool name and arguments; approving executes and resumes, denying returns an error the agent can work against.

multi-tenancy.note: Identity objects and agent tags associate agents with end users, but the open-source server documents no org or project permission boundary and warns against exposing it to untrusted clients.

declarative-deployment.note: Declarative fleet management with version-controlled YAML comes from lettactl, a community-built CLI listed under community guides rather than a first-party feature.

agent-versioning.note: Official template versioning with migrate and rollback is labeled cloud-only and deprecated, so self-hosted rollout control comes from the community lettactl tool.

skill-learning.note: Agents have a built-in skill creator and write skills into their own git-backed memory filesystem, persisting them as part of agent identity across agent, project, and computer scopes.
